findings.title: The frozen evidence does not prove the authorized full-record load or narrow case-summary publication boundary
evidence: dist/web/src/features/case-queue/components/case-intake.tsx imports useCaseIntakeProjection and useCaseDetail, but the implementations of those hooks, their API clients, and their response models are absent from the 114-entry source manifest.

dist/web/src/features/case-queue/components/case-intake.test.tsx mocks both hooks and supplies a hand-built narrow summary plus a hand-built full record. It proves that the route preserves the exact guidance and focuses Plan key after those mocked values are supplied; it does not exercise a tenant/capability-authorized full-record request or the real summary projection.

dist/web/src/features/case-queue/components/case-detail.test.tsx also mocks useCaseDetailProjection and its mock object includes memberId, procedureCode, and planKey. No retained assertion verifies that the actual case-summary response omits those fields.

dist/validate.py marks incomplete-input-recovery Passed from string presence, mocked focus tests, and red/restore logs. It never inspects or executes the missing production projection/full-record boundary, so its statement that intake loads an authorized full record without widening the summary exceeds the frozen evidence.
findings.impact: Two explicit focused Web-03 requirements remain unsupported: focus must occur only after an authorized full-record load, and the case-summary publication must remain narrow. The UI behavior after data injection is proven, but the security/publication boundary that supplies that data is not.
findings.required_correction: Freeze the production case-summary projection and full-record hook/API path, then retain a mounted local integration check showing that the summary response omits memberId, planKey, and procedureCode while the full-record request enforces verified tenant and capability scope before the first-missing-field focus is derived. Rebuild the manifest and rerun final review against its new digest.

checks_performed: Computed SHA-256 of dist/source-manifest.sha256 and observed the required digest 57a23c177f126be71e20b7306fe1eee7999af237d67931b1cc26fe6cd97fe55a.
Ran SHA-256 verification from dist and observed OK for all 114 frozen entries.
Executed dist/validate.py and observed result Passed with all 15 validator checks Passed.

Independently reviewed the frozen OpenSpec proposal, design, specification, tasks, result, review narrative, validator, SQL migrations, Rust AppServices/routes/adapter snapshots, browser model/API/hook/store/panel/case-detail/intake/form snapshots, focused tests, command receipt, red/restore receipts, and completion evidence.

Confirmed the frozen server mutation accepts only commandId and expectedCaseInputRevision; five states and temporal intersection rules are implemented; practice/capability refusal is layered; invalidation and durable command reconciliation are retained; the panel is mounted in CaseDetail with responsive/accessibility classes; no desktop or mobile path is present; the administering-entity feature contains no TanStack Query, SWR, or Apollo cache import; and actual-browser/full case-to-letter certification is explicitly assigned to Web-17.
rationale: The artifact supports the core server-authoritative resolution, temporal, refusal, invalidation, reconciliation, mounted component, scope, and deferral claims. A required security and publication claim depends on production files that are neither frozen nor exercised: the only retained destination test replaces both data-loading boundaries with mocks. Because the requested focused boundary expressly includes authorization-before-focus and narrow summary publication, that evidence gap is material and blocks a PASS.
